interpretation_boundary: Inference-time coupled branch ablation only. Pixel disablement also removes pixel support and changes downstream morphology/support/gating; results are not pure independent encoder contributions.
research_boundary: Banks share slots and V2 TRAIN references may overlap training; no independent-test or statistical-significance claim.

explicit_answers.1_full_vs_pixel_only: Yes on B and C Black KID/FID and on B+C pooled Black KID/FID.
explicit_answers.2_full_vs_latent_only: Yes on B and C Black KID/FID and on B+C pooled Black KID/FID.
explicit_answers.3_larger_closure_effect: Closing the pixel branch and its coupled pixel-support path had the larger B+C Black KID/FID impact.
explicit_answers.4_B_C_consistency: Yes. Full had lower Black KID and FID than both single-branch variants in both B and C.
explicit_answers.5_best_pooled_black: Raw SD2 was best overall; Full was best among the three MSDF branch configurations for both A+B+C and B+C.
explicit_answers.6_best_overall: Raw SD2 was best overall in pooled Overall KID and FID; Full was best among the three MSDF branch configurations.
explicit_answers.7_full_vs_raw_gap: See full_vs_raw_ABC/full_vs_raw_BC and Overall counterparts for exact absolute and relative gaps.
explicit_answers.8_retain_dual_branch: Yes for this frozen inference configuration because Full won every declared B/C and B+C Black comparison; this does not prove a training-level architecture claim.
explicit_answers.9_training_level_ablation: Yes, a separately trained single-branch ablation is warranted to separate learned branch value from inference-time support/gate coupling. It was not started.
